stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Buys Two Miami Affordable Housing Rentals
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group, paying a combined $63.8 million, property records show. In the largest deal, the investor paid $34 million for the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments in the Naranja neighborhood, near the southern end of the county. Built in 2011, the 4.8-acre asset houses 20 three-story buildings at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court, just west of the South Dixie Highway. The sale breaks down to roughly $226,660 per unit. CBRE Capital Partners provided a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan. Across the county in Miami’s Little River neighborhood, Starwood paid $29.75 million for the 160-unit Lafayette Square complex. The 19-story building sits on a 1.2-acre site, a block west from Northeast Second Avenue at 150 Northeast 79th Street. The deal equates to about $185,900 per apartment. The Gatehouse Group appears to have retained ownership of the adjacent 136-unit property. The Mansfield, Mass.-based firm developed both the Lafayette Square and Magnolia Landing Apartments, completing the former in 2008 and the latter in 2011. Representatives for Starwood and Gatehouse Group did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Capital acquired two Miami-Dade affordable rental properties for $63.8M total.
Magnolia Landing (150 units, Naranja) and Lafayette Square (160 units, Little River) purchased.
Freddie Mac financing available; affordables remain investment-grade asset class in South Florida.
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management paid $63.8 million for two affordable housing complexes in Miami-Dade County: the 150-unit Magnolia Landing in Naranja ($34M, $226.7K/unit) and the 160-unit Lafayette Square in Little River ($29.75M, $185.9K/unit). CBRE Capital Partners arranged a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan for Magnolia. Both properties were acquired from Gatehouse Group and represent older, stabilized assets (2011 vintage and earlier).
stories.impact: Institutional investor appetite for affordable rentals in Miami-Dade signals continued GSE-backed debt availability and investor confidence in rent-restricted portfolios as counter-cyclical assets. The sub-$230K/unit basis on older construction suggests limited new supply risk in the affordable segment, which can sustain modest rent growth and cap rate stability across South Florida market.

stories.title: Ad Agency Doubles Office HQ Space in Move to Hackman Campus in L.A.
stories.excerpt: An international advertising agency is more than doubling its office footprint with a new headquarters lease in El Segundo, Calif. Innocean USA signed the 101,000-square-foot deal at Hackman Capital Partners’ creative office campus in the small enclave just south of Los Angeles International Airport. The agency will relocate nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach after construction on its new space concludes in 2027, according to JLL, which represented the tenant. The company reportedly will use part of the space as a production facility for commercials and other content. Terms of the lease were not disclosed. “This move is about creating the right environment for our next chapter,” Innocean USA CEO Steve Jun said in a statement. “This is an investment in our people, our clients, and the future we’re building together.” The complex, named after its address at 888 Douglas Street, includes four buildings totaling 550,000 square feet over 30 acres. Hackman acquired the former Northrop Grumman aerospace manufacturing complex in 2016, and invested about $100 million converting it into the creative office. Other major occupiers at the property have included L’Oréal USA, which signed for more than 100,000 square feet in 2021, and Beyond Meat, which originally leased 280,000 square feet for its headquarters. Aerospace and defense companies have also returned to L.A.’s South Bay, and helped bolster leasing at the El Segundo campus. Hypersonic aircraft developer Hermeus signed for 62,552 square feet earlier this year, while Varda Space Industries expanded to 54,749 square feet in 2025. Innocean USA is the U.S. arm of Innocean Worldwide, which was created by Hyundai Motor Group. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean, while Hackman was represented in-house. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Innocean USA leasing 101K SF at Hackman Capital's El Segundo creative office campus.
601-person headcount relocating from Huntington Beach; occupancy circa 2027.
Tenant doubling footprint; on-site production facility signals content/media cluster formation.
stories.summary: International advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot headquarters lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 550,000-SF creative office campus in El Segundo (near LAX), doubling from its current 50,000-SF Huntington Beach space. Nearly 600 employees will relocate upon project completion in 2027; the tenant will use part of the space for commercial/content production. The campus sits on 30 acres and includes four buildings on the site of a former Northrop Grumman aerospace facility.
stories.impact: Innocean's doubling-down on premium creative office in El Segundo—anchored by media production—signals sustained demand for specialized flex office in Los Angeles' aerospace/tech corridor and validates Hackman's redevelopment thesis for repurposed industrial campuses. A 600-person relocation also creates downstream demand for workforce housing (apartments, housing stock) in South Bay submarkets; watch for wage/demographic tailwinds in nearby Torrance, Manhattan Beach, and Hermosa Beach rentals.

stories.title: Attorney James Allen Joins Camber Property Group as Senior Counsel
stories.excerpt: Camber Property Group has onboarded a new general counsel for its affordable housing and community development transactions, Commercial Observer has learned. James Allen has decamped from real estate law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein and started the new role this week assisting Camber with affordable housing projects in New York state and the New York tri-state region, according to the development firm. “One trend I am seeing is that, in their efforts to solve the ongoing housing affordability crisis, more developers are starting to expand both the types of projects that they participate in and their geographic footprint,” Allen said in a statement. “Camber is always thinking creatively about both, but they present unique challenges.” Allen was previously an associate for four years at Nixon Peabody and a senior staff attorney for the New York Court of Appeals. The Brooklyn Law School graduate also pens articles about housing equity and affordability while serving on the board of the New York Housing Conference’s Rising Leaders Network and the New York City Bar Association’s Housing & Urban Development Committee. Hirschen Singer & Epstein did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “I feel lucky to have the chance to expand upon that and work with many of the legal partners that I have learned from over the years, while Camber solidifies its New York presence and intentionally expands its footprint to other regions,” Allen said. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Camber Property Group hired attorney James Allen as senior counsel for affordable housing.
Focus: affordable housing and community development in NY/tri-state region.
Executive notes developer geographic expansion trend amid affordability crisis solving.
stories.summary: Camber Property Group added James Allen as general counsel, tasked with affordable housing and community development transactions across New York state and the tri-state region. Allen, a Brooklyn Law School graduate with prior roles at Nixon Peabody and as a senior staff attorney for the New York Court of Appeals, will focus on expanding Camber's affordable portfolio. He noted that developers are increasingly broadening project types and geographic footprint to address housing affordability.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to core multifamily development. However, Allen's insight that developers are expanding into affordable and mixed-tenure projects signals a structural shift toward tax-credit and community development financing vehicles in NY/tri-state, which may compete for land and capital with market-rate development but also unlock subsidy-supported returns in constrained markets like NYC and Westchester.

stories.title: Selldorf Architects Renews 14K-SF 860 Broadway Lease for 10 Years
stories.excerpt: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects has renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at Gordon Property Group’s 860 Broadway. Selldorf has called the Flatiron District’s 860 Broadway home for the last two decades, according to landlord brokerage Colliers. The asking rent was not disclosed. However, the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $79.41 per square foot, with Class A office space asking an average of $97.22 per foot and Class B space asking $79.96 during the second quarter, according to Colliers data. Seth Hecht from Colliers represented Gordon Property in this deal, while the tenant was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss from Savills. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” Hecht said in a statement announcing the renewal. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” Savills did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. “Our focus has always been on owning and operating buildings for the long term,” Tim Gordon, managing director of Gordon Property Group, said in the statement. “Creating an environment where great companies choose to stay and grow is the ultimate measure of our success, and we’re proud that 860 Broadway continues to earn that kind of commitment.” Selldorf Architects was founded by Annabelle Selldorf in New York City in 1988, according to the company website. The firm has worked on a number of prestigious projects, including the Frick Collection, the Chateau Haut-Brion — a 16th century estate near Bordeaux in France – and the Museum of Contemporary Art in San Diego. bullets: Selldorf Architects renewed 13.8K-SF lease at Gordon Property's 860 Broadway, 10-year term.
Tenant held 20-year occupancy in Flatiron District; no renewal spread disclosed.
Midtown South Class A office averaging $97.22/SF asking; Class B $79.96/SF in Q2.
stories.summary: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at 860 Broadway in Manhattan's Flatiron District, where it has been headquartered for two decades. Asking rent was not disclosed, but Colliers data shows Midtown South Class A office space averaged $97.22 per square foot and Class B space $79.96 per square foot in Q2. The tenant's long-term commitment signals stability in the creative/design office market.
stories.impact: Minimal impact to multifamily. Long-term lease renewal by a design-focused tenant in an iconic creative office building reflects selective resilience in Manhattan office for firms with deep local roots and specialized space needs, but does not signal broader office market recovery that would affect residential demand or labor migration patterns.

stories.title: Agora Delivers 90K-SF N. Las Vegas Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Agora Realty (Agora) has completed construction for Hylo Park South, its 90,750-square-foot grocery-anchored retail center located at the southeast corner of Lake Mead Blvd. and Rancho Drive in the city of North Las Vegas. This retail center will be a central gathering place for Agora’s 73-acre master-planned, mixed-use community Hylo Park that is now in its third phase of development with approximate construction costs of $375 million. The 11-acre retail center is already 95 percent leased to many nationally recognized tenants, led by anchor tenant Cardenas Markets along with Ross Dress for Less, Starbucks, Chipotle, In N Out, PDS Health, AT&T, UPS, Chase Bank, Allstate, Sourdough & Co., and Tesla. Hylo Park South tenants will be open and operating by early 2027. In addition, Agora sold a 1.2-acre pad within Hylo Park South at the southeast corner of Rancho Drive and Lake Mead Blvd. to In-N-Out Burger for development. The post Agora Delivers 90K-SF N. Las Vegas Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Agora Realty completed Hylo Park South, 90.8K-SF retail center in North Las Vegas.
Grocery-anchored by Cardenas Markets; 95% pre-leased; phase 3 of 73-acre mixed-use.
Total project cost $375M; tenants opening early 2027; In-N-Out pad sold separately.
stories.summary: Agora Realty delivered Hylo Park South, a 90,750-square-foot grocery-anchored retail center at Lake Mead Boulevard and Rancho Drive in North Las Vegas, with 95% occupancy pre-leasing. The project is phase three of Agora's 73-acre Hylo Park mixed-use master plan with approximate construction costs of $375 million. National tenants include Cardenas Markets (anchor), Ross, Starbucks, Chipotle, In-N-Out, and Tesla; occupancy is slated for early 2027. Agora sold a 1.2-acre pad to In-N-Out for its own development.
stories.impact: Retail delivery in North Las Vegas reflects sustained population and household formation in the Las Vegas metro outskirts; the grocery+discount+QSR mix signals working-class/family demographic capture. Successful pre-leasing in a suburban retail center indicates underlying apartment demand in the submarket—developers should monitor Hylo Park's residential pipeline and demographic absorption to identify secondary-market multifamily upside in the North Las Vegas corridor as wages and employment stabilize.

stories.title: BH Picks Up Nearly 300K-SF Plano Office Park
stories.excerpt: BH Properties, a value-add real estate investment firm with regional offices in Dallas, Austin, and Houston, completed the acquisition of Tollway North Office Park, a 297,591-square-foot, seven-building business park in Plano, Texas. The acquisition follows the firm’s February 2025 purchase of the adjacent R&D at Legacy campus, bringing BH’s ownership within the Legacy Business Park to more than 675,000 square feet across fourteen buildings. BH acquired the property from KBS. KBS was represented by Newmark’s Dallas team of Gary Carr, Chris Murphy, Robert Hill, and Austin Sheahan, while BH was represented by Scott Henry, its managing director of Texas acquisitions based in Dallas. The development was built between 1998 and 2000. BH Properties plans to capitalize on the property’s leasing upside while evaluating future repositioning opportunities that reflect changing occupier preferences. Stream Realty’s Chase Lopez, James Mantzuranis, and Sam Bass in Dallas will be representing BH on leasing. The post BH Picks Up Nearly 300K-SF Plano Office Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BH Properties acquired Tollway North Office Park, 297.6K SF, seven buildings in Plano, TX.
Built 1998–2000; KBS seller; BH now owns 675K+ SF across Legacy Business Park.
Value-add strategy; BH seeking leasing upside and repositioning for occupier preferences.
stories.summary: BH Properties, a value-add investor with Dallas, Austin, and Houston offices, completed the acquisition of Tollway North Office Park, a 297,591-square-foot, seven-building business park built between 1998 and 2000 in Plano, Texas. The deal follows BH's February 2025 purchase of the adjacent R&D at Legacy campus, bringing BH's Legacy Business Park portfolio to more than 675,000 square feet across 14 buildings. BH plans to capitalize on leasing upside and evaluate repositioning to reflect changing occupier preferences.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, BH's accumulation of 675K+ SF in Plano's Legacy Business Park suggests confidence in suburban DFW office consolidation and adaptive-reuse potential; if BH pursues mixed-use redevelopment or conversion of underleased Class B office, it could unlock multifamily density in a high-growth submarket and signal labor clustering trends. Monitor Plano's population growth and wage data to assess whether office repositioning correlates with residential demand.

stories.title: Cabot Offloads 2.4M-SF Texas Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Cabot Properties sold an eight-building modern industrial portfolio totaling approximately 2.4 million square feet across Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston, Texas. The portfolio was acquired by a private real estate investment firm. Five of the properties are in the Dallas-Fort Worth submarkets of South Dallas, Alliance, DFW Airport, and Great Southwest/Arlington with an average vintage of 2015, totaling approximately two million square feet. Sustained occupier demand, declining vacancy, and improving absorption across large-format industrial space have resulted in a recent period of accelerated leasing and transactional activity in the Dallas-Fort Worth market. The additional three buildings are in Houston’s Northwest and North Corridors. The Capital Markets Teams of CBRE, Cushman & Wakefield, and Eastdil Secured represented Cabot separately across the transaction. Last week, Cabot sold a collection of 11 industrial properties totaling approximately 2.5 million square feet across key industrial submarkets in Greater Chicago and Minneapolis, Minnesota. The post Cabot Offloads 2.4M-SF Texas Industrial Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Cabot Properties sold 2.4M-SF industrial portfolio (eight buildings) across Texas.
Five buildings in DFW (South Dallas, Alliance, Airport, Southwest/Arlington; 2015 avg vintage).
Three buildings in Houston NW and North Corridors; sold to private REIF.
stories.summary: Cabot Properties sold an eight-building modern industrial portfolio totaling approximately 2.4 million square feet across Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston. Five properties are located in DFW submarkets (South Dallas, Alliance, DFW Airport, Great Southwest/Arlington) with an average vintage of 2015, totaling two million square feet. Three additional buildings are in Houston's Northwest and North Corridors. Capital Markets teams from CBRE, Cushman & Wakefield, and Eastdil Secured represented Cabot. The market context notes sustained occupier demand, declining vacancy, and improving absorption across large-format industrial.
stories.impact: Cabot's divestiture of modern industrial suggests capital rotation out of logistics and into other asset classes (likely office value-add or other repositioning plays). The sale reflects tight DFW and Houston industrial markets with strong leasing momentum; sustained occupier demand for large-format warehouse/logistics drives continued employment growth in these metros, strengthening multifamily demand, particularly for workforce/middle-income rentals near industrial corridors (South Dallas, Northwest Houston). Monitor job creation in logistics/e-commerce sectors to validate rent growth thesis.

stories.title: Mortgage Bankers Association: CRE Lending Volume Up 16% Year-Over-Year
stories.excerpt: Commercial and multifamily mortgage loan originations were 16% higher in the second quarter of 2026 than in the year-ago period, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) Quarterly Survey of Commercial/Multifamily Mortgage Bankers Originations. Dollar volume increased 12% from Q1 of 2026, MBA said. Increased originations for retail, office, hotel, industrial and multifamily properties led to an overall increase in commercial/multifamily lending volumes. Dollar volume of loans for retail properties rose 61%, while office loans rose 47%, lodging properties rose 19%, multifamily rose 8% and industrial increased 6%. Healthcare originations decreased 19% year-over-year. “Commercial and multifamily mortgage lending maintained its upward trajectory in the second quarter as improving capital markets and stronger transaction activity supported higher origination volumes,” said Reggie Booker, MBA’s associate VP of commercial research. “Office lending was strong, with increases in originations on an annual and quarterly basis, signaling renewed financing activity in a sector that has faced significant headwinds. Additionally, CMBS and bank lenders posted particularly strong gains in the second quarter. Although activity remains uneven across some capital sources and property sectors, the overall increase in lending points to continued improvement in commercial real estate finance markets.” The post Mortgage Bankers Association: CRE Lending Volume Up 16% Year-Over-Year appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MBA Q2 2026: Commercial/multifamily originations up 16% YoY; dollar volume +12% QoQ.
Multifamily loans +8% YoY; retail +61%, office +47%, lodging +19%, industrial +6%.
CMBS and bank lenders posted strong gains; healthcare originations -19% YoY.
stories.summary: The Mortgage Bankers Association's Quarterly Survey of Commercial/Multifamily Mortgage Bankers Originations reports that commercial and multifamily mortgage loan originations were 16% higher in Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025, with dollar volume up 12% from Q1 2026. Multifamily originations rose 8% year-over-year, trailing retail (61%), office (47%), and lodging (19%), while industrial rose 6%. Healthcare originations declined 19% year-over-year. CMBS and bank lenders posted particularly strong gains, signaling improved capital market conditions and renewed financing activity.
stories.impact: Multifamily lending growth of 8% YoY, while positive, lags retail (+61%) and office (+47%), suggesting capital still favors retail and office repositioning deals over new multifamily starts. The broader 16% Y-o-Y increase in CRE originations and Q1-to-Q2 12% quarterly jump indicate thawing credit conditions and improving cap rates—developers should monitor whether falling rates and rising transaction volume unlock new multifamily starts or primarily fuel acquisitions of stabilized assets. Watch for divergence between CMBS/bank appetite; bank focus on office may signal stricter multifamily underwriting on marginal markets.

stories.title: Valley National Bank Provides $30M Value-Add Refi for Park Towers in Miami
stories.excerpt: Moshe Popack’s YMP Real Estate Management has secured $30 million to refinance Park Towers, a 210-unit multifamily complex in Miami, Commercial Observer can first report. Valley National Bank provided the loan, structured at a fixed-rate of 6.09 percent, while Meridian Capital Group’s David Hayum and Michael Farkovits arranged the transaction. Meridian’s Hyum noted in a statement that Popack, a third-generation real estate investor, and the YMP management team have owned and operated Park Towers for more than a decade and have engaged in a concentrated value-add strategy, investing capital improvements into the property for several years. “Valley National Bank recognized that track record, stayed engaged throughout the process, and delivered a financing solution that met the borrower’s objectives,” added Hyum. Park Towers is located at 777 North West 155th Lane in the Biscayne Gardens section of Miami, near both University of Miami and Florida International University. The 224,519-square-foot apartment building opened in 1973. The 10-story building is a mix of studios, one-bedrooms and two-bedrooms and has undergone capital improvements since YMP purchased the asset in 2012. YMP Management has emerged as a player in the Sun Belt in recent years and now owns more than 4,000 multifamily units across Florida, Georgia and North Carolina. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Valley National Bank provided $30M value-add refi for YMP's Park Towers, Miami, 210 units.
Fixed-rate 6.09%; Meridian Capital arranged; property near University of Miami/FIU.
Owner/operator invested capital improvements for over a decade; third-generation investor.
stories.summary: Moshe Popack's YMP Real Estate Management refinanced Park Towers, a 210-unit multifamily complex in Miami's Biscayne Gardens section (near University of Miami and Florida International University), with a $30 million loan from Valley National Bank at a fixed rate of 6.09 percent. Meridian Capital Group's David Hayum and Michael Farkovits arranged the transaction. YMP has owned and operated the property for more than a decade, pursuing a concentrated value-add strategy with ongoing capital improvements.
stories.impact: Valley National's willingness to execute a 6.09% fixed-rate refi for a stabilized, value-add asset with a proven operator signals improving financing conditions in South Florida multifamily and regional bank appetite for seasoned properties with demonstrated NOI growth. The Biscayne Gardens location (near two universities) suggests sustained student/young-professional housing demand; similar university-proximate assets in Miami may see refinancing tailwinds, improving cap rate compression for value-add sellers.

stories.title: RXR-Led Team Lands Construction Financing for 301-Unit Denver Rental Community
stories.excerpt: RXR, together with Halpern Real Estate Investments, Korman Communities and Invent Development Partners, secured $125 million in construction financing for AVE Station House, a 301-unit luxury multifamily development in Denver, Colorado. The property was financed with a $100 million senior loan from Madison Realty Capital and a $25 million mezzanine loan from an insurance company. The development comprises 271 market-rate apartments and 30 affordable units, along with more than 6,200 square feet of ground-floor retail space and approximately 290 secured parking spaces. Upon completion, AVE Station House will offer a mix of studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom residences. Each apartment will feature work-from-home spaces. Residents will have access to an extensive amenity package including a rooftop pool and lounge, fitness center, spa with sauna and steam. JLL Capital Markets’ Debt Advisory team, led by Leon McBroom, Michael Gigliotti, Will Haass and Ellie Savage, represented the borrower, as well as Paul Patafio of Hudson Realty Capital, who represented the borrower in arranging financing for the project The post RXR-Led Team Lands Construction Financing for 301-Unit Denver Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RXR/Halpern/Korman/Invent secured $125M construction financing for AVE Station House, Denver.
301-unit luxury (271 market-rate, 30 affordable); ground-floor retail; 290 parking spaces.
Madison Realty $100M senior + $25M mezzanine from insurance company; completion TBD.
stories.summary: RXR, Halpern Real Estate Investments, Korman Communities, and Invent Development Partners secured $125 million in construction financing for AVE Station House, a 301-unit luxury multifamily development in Denver. The capital stack comprises a $100 million senior loan from Madison Realty Capital and a $25 million mezzanine loan from an insurance company. The project includes 271 market-rate units, 30 affordable units, 6,200+ square feet of ground-floor retail, and 290 secured parking spaces, with amenities including rooftop pool, fitness center, and spa. JLL Capital Markets and Hudson Realty Capital arranged the financing.
stories.impact: Successful construction financing for a 301-unit mixed-tenure development (91% market-rate, 10% affordable) at a 4:1 senior-to-mezz ratio indicates strong lender confidence in Denver's rental fundamentals and investor appetite for mixed-income communities with retail/mixed-use components. The use of insurance-company mezzanine capital suggests institutional confidence in completion risk; developers should view Denver as an open market for new supply with favorable financing conditions. The AVE project's size and financing profile suggest comparable Denver submarkets can support new-build development at moderate-to-low yields (likely 4–5% stabilized cap rates), which may compress returns for value-add players but validate underlying demand strength.
